frames.title: isorite in the terminal
frames.text: OpenCode, an agent that writes code, with your notes beside it: a developer's notes on an N-body simulation, and an empty folder for the code. The browser that opened is the other half, on the same notes. The model is scripted. Press enter to open.

frames.title: Ask for code
frames.text: The prompt is filled in. Press enter. Before it writes, the agent looks in your notes: by words, by meaning, and along their links. OpenCode asks before it writes a file: allow it.
frames.does: press enter, and allow the write

frames.title: Notes in play
frames.text: On the right: what it found, what it reached from there, and what it used, in gold. Its answer cites your notes, [1] and the section. In the browser, the Atlas draws the same path as it goes. Type /next.

frames.title: More, from your notes
frames.text: Press enter. It reads your notes on Barnes–Hut and the quadtree, writes the code, and adds to your note on the goal where the code now is. The code is OpenCode's, as always; what it would change in a note waits for you.
frames.does: press enter, and allow the write

frames.title: isorite's tools
frames.text: What it used are isorite's: brief_base, search_notes, find_similar, outline_note and read_note to look, propose_note_edit and propose_note_write to suggest. And two commands: /atlas and /note. Type /next.

frames.title: One note's atlas
frames.text: Type /atlas barnes hut. Beside the chat: what the note requires, on the left, and what builds on it, on the right.

frames.title: Open the note
frames.text: Type /note two galaxies. A note in the terminal: who wrote each paragraph in the gutter, maths as source, links underlined.

frames.title: Keep it, or not
frames.text: The agent's change waits between dotted lines. [k] keeps it, [e] edits it first, [r] removes it; [n] goes to the next.

frames.title: Ask Iso here
frames.text: ↑ and ↓ choose a paragraph; [/] asks Iso, isorite's own agent, to write after it. Its answer waits for you the same way.

frames.title: Every change is kept
frames.text: [t] lists the note's history. Choose a moment to see the note as it was then; [q] comes back to now.

frames.title: Send it to the agent
frames.text: [s] sends the paragraph the cursor is on to the agent, with what you want of it. It waits under "from you" for your next prompt.
frames.does: press q, then s, and say what you want

frames.title: That is the terminal
frames.text: On your own base: isorite term <base>. Point it at a model with ISORITE_GATEWAY_URL, or use OpenCode's own. /tour hides this card, /next closes it.
